item.title: Owens Reframes Kirk Assassination: Owens says grief fuels spiritual mission; video blends faith and audience engagement
item.description: Candace Owens has opened up about how her feelings changed following Charlie Kirk’s assassination. She said she has moved beyond the initial trauma and no longer feels haunted, instead believing Kirk is spiritually “fighting alongside” her. Owens connected her optimism to her belief that truth will prevail and said she feels Charlie is still with them. She also encouraged viewers to support her show by purchasing merchandise.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Amazon AI Opt-Out Backlash: Twitch auto-enables training on streams; creators must change privacy settings
item.description: Twitch is facing criticism over a new setting that allows Amazon to use streamer content for generative AI training by default. Streamers can opt out through their privacy settings. Users questioned why the option was not turned off unless creators agreed. Twitch said it is not training GenAI models itself, but the setting covers Amazon’s AI model training.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Old Graduation Clip Resurfaces: Clavicular’s virtual ceremony goes viral; fans see quieter past
item.description: A resurfaced video from Clavicular’s COVID-era middle school graduation has gone viral, giving fans a wholesome glimpse of the streamer before his rise to internet fame. The footage shows his name being announced during a virtual ceremony while his parents celebrate from home. Now 20, Clavicular has built a large following through IRL streams, looksmaxxing content and controversial online discussions, making the old clip especially surprising for fans.

item.title: Paranormal Creator’s Fatal Crash: Jiang Xiaorou dies after July accident; family urges fans to stop speculation
item.description: Jiang Xiaorou, a 24-year-old Chinese paranormal content creator, died on August 10 after suffering severe injuries in a July 15 traffic accident. Known for challenging superstition, she had more than 1.28 million Douyin followers. Her controversial videos, including one showing her destroying a Guanyin statue, resurfaced after her death. However, there is no evidence linking her accident to supernatural punishment, despite speculation circulating online.

item.title: Quote by Karl Popper: 'Those who promise us paradise on earth never produced anything but a hell'
item.description: Karl Popper highlighted the dangers of striving for a perfect society, warning that such aspirations frequently lead to disastrous outcomes. He pointed out how leaders driven by utopian dreams tend to accumulate excessive power, often resulting in brutality. The French Revolution and several authoritarian regimes serve as stark illustrations of this trend. In the current era, technological advancements and corporate ideologies can echo these same pitfalls.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by Zeno: 'We have two ears and one mouth, so we should listen more than we say'
item.description: Zeno of Citium, originally a Phoenician trader, established Stoicism in the heart of ancient Athens. He advocated that true listening is an intentional skill rather than simply a precursor to responding. This timeless philosophy champions the value of understanding prior to action. Contemporary studies validate that active listening boosts trust and mitigates conflict, emphasizing the age-old design of our auditory and vocal apparatus.

item.title: In 1962, New Jersey took a family's property; they challenged the price and were awarded $350,000
item.description: Exploring vintage postcards reveals a fascinating glimpse into coastal life in early New Jersey. Historian John Joseph Patrick Mulhern recounted his experiences on Sandy Hook, describing the thrilling days of tracking ships and conducting groundbreaking radio experiments. He vividly portrayed the operations of the Navesink lighthouses and the evolving landscape, showcasing the rich maritime heritage and community growth of the time.

item.title: James, 18, Earl of Wessex, passes A-levels, to study at Royal Agricultural University
item.description: James, 18, Earl of Wessex, has passed his A-levels and will study rural land management at the Royal Agricultural University in Gloucestershire. Prince Edward and Sophie’s son spent part of the summer working as a farmhand at King Charles III’s Sandringham estate, where he was reportedly seen driving tractors and embracing hands-on work.

item.title: She spent 10 months restoring a 160-year-old house; now Lauren Iraeta is reconnecting families...
item.description: Lauren Iraeta approached her home renovation as a journey through time, merging creativity with historical inquiry. By delving into neglected family records and tales from earlier occupants, she uncovered names etched within the widow's walk. This captivating endeavor brought descendants closer to their ancestors' cherished childhood narratives, illuminating the profound history woven into these aged abodes.

item.title: In June 2026, Washington began restoring 270 acres across two river islands; the project will...
item.description: In June 2026, heavy machinery commenced work on a significant coastal restoration initiative. The plan involves the dismantling of outdated sea defenses and the breaching of river levees on two islands, aiming to transform 270 acres of previously cultivated land into natural intertidal wetlands. This restoration will create critical habitats for juvenile Puget Sound Chinook salmon, with the completion date set for autumn 2028.

item.title: Meet Scarlett Tiani, the Connecticut student whose dog-safety invention reached US Nationals
item.description: In a remarkable achievement, Connecticut student Scarlett Tiani has garnered national attention for her inventive pet safety solution, Tail Wag Warning. Designed to enhance safety during unexpected dog interactions, Tiani's creation received numerous accolades at the prestigious national Invention Convention. With legal support at her side, she is now set to embark on the journey of securing a U.S. patent for her groundbreaking invention.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Jimmy Chilimigras, the Mississippi teen who finished high school at 12
item.description: At just 18 years old, James Chilimigras has achieved remarkable academic milestones, having graduated from Loyola University New Orleans College of Law, where he ranked in the top two percent of his class while earning five certificates. Displaying an exceptional intellect, he completed both his bachelor's and master’s degrees by the age of 15 and became the youngest Certified Public Accountant in history.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Michigan's historic Ford House is replacing concrete shoreline with natural habitat
item.description: A groundbreaking initiative along Michigan's Lake St. Clair is reshaping the shoreline into thriving natural wetlands. By dismantling decades of concrete barriers, this project endeavors to create essential habitats for local fish populations. The transformation revolves around the historic Edsel and Eleanor Ford Estate, aiming to revitalize coastal marshes while boosting biodiversity and community education on ecosystem preservation.
